# Top 5 posts from r/moviecritic day

## 1. This scene at the end of “Crazy,Stupid,Love” ruins this entire movie for me

**Score:** 1596
**Body:** You have a wonderfully unique romantic comedy all the way up until the finish line where the movie face plants so hard it shatters all of its teeth. The plot was doing such a good job of deconstructing and critiquing the idea of “never stopping to get with the person you desire” by making the 13 year old boy realize that repeatedly pursuing someone that’s not interested in you is actually really shitty but the moment he comes to this conclusion his dad immediately undoes all the boys character development by telling him that he’s wrong and that he should never give up on love. This leads to the 17 year old girl finally caving to the whims of this 13 year old boy and GIVING HIM SEVERAL POLAROID NUDES OF HERSELF TO HIM. It’s actually genuinely disturbing to me and leaves such a bad taste in my mouth that I really don’t think I can recommend the movie even though 95% of it is really good. Not only does it perpetuate the very dangerous notion that you shouldn’t take no for an answer in your romantic pursuits, it also seems completely fine with this pedophilic/grooming behavior. Yikes. 

### Top 6 comments and their replies (up to depth 10)

1. who is this… David Lindhagen?
  - Lindhăgen… 
2. TIL r/moviecritic isn't a place for being critical of movies.
  - No fighting in the war room!
3. YO WTF IS THIS THREAD LOL. Do yall even *like* movies? Or is it just pretty colors and loud noises to you? What the hell is this aversion to analysis in a movie critic sub of all places?
  - I’ve been yelled at and downvoted in 6 different subs in just today pointing out how there is no longer any discussions when someone brings up some criticism, they just get yelled at and told “don’t watch it then!” “Don’t buy it then!”

Something sick is going on, and it’s either bots or people critical thinking are deteriorating so fast that they don’t know how to have discussions anymore. 
    - I watched an Instagram video today of a guy saying how valuable blockbuster was because at least we’d take the film home and commit to watching it. If we didn’t like it, we’d still usually watch it til the end and at least have valid reasons to criticize it. 

Nowadays we (broadly speaking) get bored of a film we’re watching on streaming sites after 10 minutes, change it, and claim it was shit. 

That sucks

Unrelated, but what’re the chances 
  - High because it's all bots on this website 
5. I agree.  The entire film kinda seems to be telling us that relationships are complicated and sometimes you just need to move on instead of obsessing over your first love and then the last 15-30 mins becomes a weird "first love always triumphs" story. This is bad writing and can't be excused by saying "heck, it's just a film, bro". This would be like if Star Wars showed everything from the perspective of the rebels and acted like their cause was just. Only to have a character talk about how hard it is to govern and how the Empire is trying their best in the last 15-30 mins and complete try to pivot the sympathy their way.

## 4. What are some of your favourite films where the soundtrack is as iconic and intense as the movie itself. I'll go first:

**Score:** 90
**Body:** Oppenheimer (2023).

The soundtrack by Ludwig Göransson is a brilliant symphony of all these deep, reflective moments punctuated by these orchestral high notes as J. Robert Oppenheimer gets closer to making the atomic bomb a reality in the movie!

Honestly, it's one of those scores that tries to convey what the man behind one of the most powerful weapons in the world was going through. Even when he is visualising the true extent of the chain reaction, the blend of instruments, along with the sharp melody, makes the scene come alive, in my opinion.

# Top 5 posts from r/TrueFilm day

## 1. iTunes vs 4k Blu, where do you see the difference

**Score:** 19
**Body:** I am currently buying 4k iTunes movies to watch on appletv 4k, and also 4 bluray for my ub450. 

I know there is always a quality difference, but I am wondering where you usually see the actual differences. Dark scene? Action scenes? Lots of fine moving details? 

Are drama movies more suited for iTunes that horror for example? 

Considering limited shelf space and that I can get a lot of 4k movies for 4€ on iTunes, I would like to make some economical choices

### Top 9 comments and their replies (up to depth 10)

1. Economical choice would be to remux it.

But to answer your question; all of the above. Your blacks would be better, the image will be less blurry during any form of movement, overall clarity of the image, etc. Even the worst looking 4K blurays will still be better than 4K digital.

It seems a shame to waste your UB450, but if you've primarily purchased on iTunes then I would say stay digital. Ignorance is bliss in this situation and will save you lots of money in the end. Remember that your iTunes purchases aren't ownership, only licenses. They can be revoked at any time while physical media can't be.
2. The difference is insane.

Me and my flatmate (who knows jack all about 4ks) tested it, I bought Alien on Apple TV, 4k dolby vision, and played the 4k disc in my ub820 for some comparing.

Bro, even I was taken aback. My flatmate literally said "they're lying! bastards" about Apple. Because it's true, if you compare the two sources back to back on a good 4k OLED TV the difference is astonishing. Just do it and you'll see, and you'll never want to watch a great film on digital again. And you will despise the streaming companies for their fake 4k badges.

Fyi the bit rate is about 20% of a true 4k film, often less.
  - The biggest difference is the audio tbh. 
3. Because no one is mentioning the hardware angle: if you're watching blu-rays on a cheaper LCD television the quality difference coud be less pronounced. Same with a smaller screen of longer viewing distance.
4. I encourage people to move back to physical media when possible. I agree about both cost and shelf space, but if I'm paying for a movie, I want to own it.

Some good news, though: many Blu-ray and 4K releases come with a digital code these days. Where you can redeem them varies, but when a code is available, in my experience, Apple is one of the choices. Better yet, more and more studios are signing on to Movies Anywhere, which is a service where you can redeem your code and then link your accounts like Apple and Amazon Prime so that your purchase shows up in \*all\* of them. So depending on the movie, you may not have to make a choice: you can have the disc, \*and\* you can have your streaming copy, without having to pay twice. I actively seek out discs with this option when they're available.
5. Streaming compression with older, grainy films is especially bad to my eyes. Even with high bitrate ethernet the compression is so aggressive that fine detail turns to mush. Lots of chroma banding and blocking in dark areas and deep reds.

Also the audio typically sounds quite thin compared to the lossless tracks on 4K discs. I tried watching Titanic via Apple TV on my Atmos surround system last April and wound up switching over to the physical UHD due to the anemic itunes sound quality.
  - Got a specific example of a title with bad chroma banding and blocking on iTunes 4k HDR vs disc? 
6. To be honest I dont see much of a difference and even if there is one (which there for sure is as we know), I dont think about that stuff when watching a movie. I just watch it. 

I have bought a lot of movies on Apple over the years and never had any issues with it. But keep in my mind, if you really want to own the movie, you should still buy the disc. 
7. Gradient lighting looks worse streamed than on BluRay. That's the biggest one for me personally. If you are watching in a home theater the audio will generally be technically better on disc V stream, but it's not very noticable.
8. Even Blu Ray discs look better than "4k" streaming, imo. Colours are richer, blacks are blacker and don't artifact in the blocky way you can still get on streams. The resolution is only one part of image quality - the bitrate for a 4k disc is far superior to streaming and more predictable and stable. The sound from the discs is also noticeably improved. Both work, but the difference when you watch a 4k disc is pretty significant in my experience. 

I do a combination of streaming and disc, which I'm sure is true for a lot of people. There are films that I really *want* on a 4k disc - *Lawrence of Arabia, 2001 A Space Odyssey –* and so I'll buy those. I don't need to have *The Sheep Detectives* in 4k...
